segments: Jubilee 17 {OCR?}.
Arab kings.
They abandoned Amida and departed.
And Sharaf al-Dawla went out,
and he went to Callinicus.
At this time, when the kingdom of the Greeks was weakened,
and the Turks were raiding from every place,
certain Armenian men of valour also joined together,
and became a band of about fifty men;
and they too were going in and plundering.
And while they were in the region of Marash,
a certain young man, likewise an Armenian, whose name was Philaretus, met them.
And when they saw that he was valiant, astute, and eager to plunder and to kill,
they took him along with them,
and he became their guide and leader.
And they began to seize secretly certain fortified places in the region of Cilicia,
and they became a large force.
And when the emperor of the Romans heard [of this],
he sent him gifts.
And Philaretus himself went to Constantinople,
and the Greeks rejoiced over him,
and they gave him gold and weapons,
and invested him as sebastos.
And he went out and ruled over Cilicia and Antioch;
and he grew strong and took also Marash, Kesum, Ra'ban, Edessa, the region of the Jihan, and Melitene.
And there were also Persian and Turkish men in his service and with him, together with the Armenians.
And because he was very oppressive,
he laid his hand upon the notables of Antioch,
and took their possessions,
and divided [them] among the troops that were with him.
And for this reason the Antiochenes hated him,
and he too hated them.
And he set over them a governor, a Persian man whose name was Isma'il,
and he left and departed from it.
Then Sulayman, the son of Qutalmish, who was killed in the capital city {OCR?} as we have said,
when he heard that Philaretus had turned aside,
prepared ships for himself,
because he had already taken Antartus and Tarsus,
and he came against Antioch from the side of the mountain and seized it,
while that Persian governor lent him assistance.
And he opened the great church of Cassian (that of Saint Cassian the Martyr?),
and took from it the treasure and the vessels of gold and silver,
and the rest of the deposits of the citizens in great quantity;
and he turned the church into a mosque.
And he proclaimed peace in the city,
and lifted the sword,
and restrained the Turks from entering the house of any of the Christians,
or taking [any] of their daughters, even in betrothal,
